and revenues, which it said reflects the strength of the tanker market, where tight supply, strong refinery margins, and geopolitical disruptions have pushed freight rates higher.

said it ordered four more newbuildings in China and South Korea, lifting its tanker construction program to six ships worth $525.9M, with options for two additional suezmaxes that would take the company's newbuilding pipeline to eight vessels if exercised.
The company said it booked two aframax/LR2 tankers at an unnamed Chinese yard and two suezmaxes at a South Korean shipbuilder, with all four vessels scheduled for delivery in 2030.
had already secured two suezmax resale newbuildings in South Korea earlier this year, paying a combined $190M for vessels due in 2027.
Teekay entered the latest acquisitions with a sizeable cash cushion, reporting $1.42B in cash and short-term investments at the end of September and no debt.
The company said its Q4 spot bookings to date averaged $272K/day for suezmaxes and $208.3K/day for aframax/LR2 vessels, with CEO Kenneth Hvid pointing to the potential for record full-year results.
